# User guide: Health, Activity and troubleshooting

## In plain words

The plugin watches itself and tells you when something needs a look. The **Health** dot at the top of the Settings page shows if the plugin is well. The **Activity tray** at the bottom right of the page lists what the plugin is doing now: installs, storage jobs, workspace starts and jobs that wait for you. It also groups repeated refused agent actions into a short-lived record. The **Debug Console** holds the plugin log and the tools that help you report a problem. When you install a new plugin version, a banner offers to reload your open pages and reconnect your terminals. Your agents and their conversations keep running through all of this.

## Where to find it

- **Health**: the dot and the word "Health" at the right end of the tab bar on **Settings**, **AI CLI Agents**.
- **Activity tray**: the pill at the bottom right of the Settings page and of the terminal page. The pill is hidden while nothing happens.
- **Debug Console**: the last tab in **Settings**, **AI CLI Agents**.
- **Update banner**: at the top of the terminal page, after an install.
- **Storage tidy-up banner**: above the terminal on the terminal page, while the storage needs a tidy-up.

## Health

### How to read the dot

1. Look at the right end of the tab bar. The dot has one of three colours. The word beside it reads **Health: ok**, **Health: warn** or **Health: fail**.
2. Press the (i) button next to the dot. On a desktop you can also hold the pointer over it. Expect: a panel opens under the tab bar. It says what the colours mean. Below that it says "All checks are OK.", or it lists each check that is not fine, with a message. Press the (i) again, or press Escape, to close the panel. A phone has no hover, so use the (i).
3. Press **Open the Debug Console** in the panel, or press the dot. Expect: the Debug Console opens.

| Colour | Word | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Green | ok | Every check is fine. |
| Amber | warn | Something deserves a look before it turns into a problem. You can keep working. |
| Red | fail | Something is broken and needs your attention. |
| Grey | unknown or "checking" | The plugin has not read its health yet. |

The overall colour is the worst result of all checks. The page reads the health again every minute. The plugin also checks itself in the background every 30 minutes. When the result gets worse, the plugin sends one Unraid notification that lists the checks that are not fine. It stays silent while the same problem remains. It sends no message when the problem ends. The plugin also publishes health changes to the Relay (see [Agent Relay](relay.md)).

### The checks, in plain words

| Check | What it looks at | Warn when | Fail when | What to do |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **supervisor** | The background program that saves and merges storage layers (the supervisor). | Never. | It does not run, it has no heartbeat file, or the heartbeat is older than three ticks (15 seconds by default). A supervisor that you turned off by configuration counts as ok. | Open the Debug Console and look for supervisor lines. |
| **manifest** | The list of saved layers that the plugin keeps. | The list comes from a newer plugin version. | The list cannot be read, or the boot check marks a home or an agent as lost or unmanaged. | Open **Settings, Storage**. See [Home and agent storage](storage.md). Restore from a backup when the home is lost. |
| **mounts** | Homes and agents that are mounted now. | Never. | A mounted home or agent has saved layers that the list does not know. | Open **Settings, Storage** to see the state of each home and agent. Send a support bundle if it stays red. |
| **defer_markers** | Storage jobs that were put off. | A put-off marker is older than 6 hours. | Never. | Look at the Activity tray for a waiting job and its reason. |
| **disk_space** | Free space on the boot drive (the USB flash drive) and use of `/tmp` (the RAM disk). | The boot drive has less than 10% free, or `/tmp` is more than 80% used. | The boot drive has less than 5% free. | Free space on the boot drive. Move homes and agents to a pool (see [Home and agent storage](storage.md)). |
| **boot_integrity** | A check of all storage at start-up. | It reports a warning state. | It reports a critical state. | Open **Settings, Storage** and read the state of each home and agent. |
| **debug_log** | The size of the plugin log. | The log is more than twice its size limit (5 MB by default). | Never. | Press the eraser icon in the Debug Console to clear the log. |
| **client_errors** | Errors that the browser pages report. | More than 10 in the last hour. | Never. | Reload the page. If it comes back, send a support bundle. |
| **storage_jobs** | The list of storage jobs. | A job failed. | Never. | Open the Debug Console and look for the error. See [Home and agent storage](storage.md). |
| **push** | Live updates to your browser. | More than 5 live updates failed in the last hour. | The channel for live updates is missing. | Reload the page. If it stays red, send a support bundle. |
| **pinned_layers** | Deleted layers that still hold space on the boot drive. | They hold 512 MB or more. The message names the workspaces that still use an old copy of the home. | Never. | Restart the workspaces that the message names. The space returns when they restart. If the message names none, the space returns at the next server restart. The check only reads. It never restarts anything. |
| **home_upper** | The writable layer of a home that lives on the boot drive. | The boot drive is 70% used or more, and a writable layer on it holds 512 MB or more. | Never. | Merge the home (**Consolidate** in the Storage tab), move the writable layer to RAM, or move homes off the boot drive. A merge closes open workspaces. |
| **agent_versions** | The version of each agent that runs, against the version that the **Agent Store** shows. The plugin reads the version from the agent's program folder. It checks only agents that install as a package. An agent that is a single program file is not checked. It skips an agent while an install or upgrade for it runs, or while its new version waits to go live. | An agent runs an older version than the Agent Store shows. A newer version is not a problem. The message reads, for example, "Gemini CLI runs version 0.46.0, which is older than version 0.65.0 that the Agent Store shows. An old writable layer can hide the new version. Choose Reinstall for the agent in the Agent Store. When the agent mounts the new version, the plugin sets the old writable layer aside and removes it after seven days." | Never. | Open the **Agent Store** and choose **Reinstall** for the agent that the message names. When the agent then mounts the new version, the plugin sets the old writable layer aside. It removes that layer seven days later. The plugin does the same for any other writable layer that no version uses. |

Four more checks appear only when they apply.

| Check | Appears when | Warn when | What to do |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **voice** | You set a voice engine address. | The last attempt to make speech failed. The message gives the reason. | Check that the engine runs. See [Voice](voice.md). |
| **voice_input** | You set a transcription address. | The last transcription failed. | Check that the engine runs and that its model is installed. |
| **backup** | A home has a backup folder. | The newest copy is older than twice the schedule interval (7 days when the schedule is off), or the last restore failed. This check never turns red. | Run a backup, or fix the target. See [Home backup and restore](backup-restore.md). |
| **favourites** | The favourites file was damaged. | The plugin set the damaged file aside. | Add your favourites again. |

If a check cannot run, it shows warn with the message "check errored". The other checks still run.

## The Activity tray

### What you see

The pill at the bottom right counts what is going on. Its text lists the parts, for example "2 tasks running, 1 failed, 1 waiting". The dot changes colour for the most urgent part. On a phone (640 pixels wide or less) the pill shows only the dot and a number. Press the pill to open the panel. The panel is titled **Activity**. The pill stays above the phone keys, so it never covers them.

Each row has three parts, and each part has one job:

- **The title** says what happened, in plain words, and names the thing by its name: "Notebook page updated: Test plan", "Installing Claude Code", "Saving home: root", "Delete workspace "my-project"?". It never starts with a workspace name and never shows an internal id.
- **The grey line** says where, who, or what comes next: the current step of a job ("Copying files"), who made a change ("by Codex CLI in model-eval"), or what to do after a failure ("Open the workspace and press Restart"). It never repeats the state.
- **The person line** appears when you did the thing yourself in the web page. It reads "by root (John)": your Unraid login, then the name you set in **Your name in the records** (Settings, **General**, part **Advanced**). A row you approved or rejected reads "approved by root (John)" or "rejected by root (John)". A row that an agent or the system made has no person line, and an older row has none either.
- **The chip** shows the state of work that is still going on. A finished record of a change (an agent updated a page, a continue was scheduled, a store was deleted) shows the time instead ("just now", "4 min ago"), because it has no state to report.

| State (chip) | What it means | Buttons |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **running** | The job works now. | **Cancel**, only on a job that Cancel can stop (an install) |
| **stalled** | The job sent no sign of life for 2 minutes. If it sends one later, it returns to running. | **Cancel**, **Dismiss** |
| **failed** | The job stopped. The red line is one sentence; the grey line says what to do. Technical detail is in the Debug Console log. | **Dismiss**, and **Retry** for a failed start. A failed row that has only **Dismiss** disappears after 5 minutes; the event list in the Debug Console keeps it. A row that needs you stays until you dismiss it: a failed start with **Retry**, a storage move that needs attention, an upgrade stopped by a server restart. |
| **waiting** | The job did its part and waits for something outside, with no time limit. For example a merge waits for room, or an agent upgrade waits for the last old session to close. The grey line gives the reason. | **Dismiss** |
| **needs approval** | An agent proposed a destructive job. The title is the question; the full statement of what approval does sits under it. See [Plugin management tools for agents](agent-tools.md). | **Approve**, **Reject** |
| **done** | The job finished. The grey line shows a result only when there is one to show ("14 agents in 6 s"). | none; the row disappears after 60 seconds. |

A Relay notice that waits shows as "Message waiting for <workspace>", with "from <sender> · held because …" under it, and the buttons **Go to**, **Force inject** (or **Press Enter**) and **Dismiss**. See [Agent Relay](relay.md). A page that an agent changed in your Notebook shows with an **Open note** button; several changes within ten seconds fold into one row, "2 Notebook pages updated", that lists the page titles.

### What appears in the tray

- Installs and upgrades of agents.
- Storage jobs: saving a home, merging layers, moving storage.
- A workspace start, but only when nobody watched it or it went wrong. A start that you began by a click shows a row only if it runs for more than 10 seconds. A reconnect to an agent that still runs shows no row.
- A failed auto-launch, with **Retry**.
- Changes that an agent made through the plugin management tools, for example "Setting changed: Voice speed to 1.2" with "by Claude Code in my-project" under it.
- Refused agent actions appear together in one record row for each workspace and 10-minute period. The title gives the count, agent and workspace, for example "3 refused calls by Claude Code in Builder". The row disappears after 60 seconds.
- Calls from one workspace after the first 20 calls to the same tool in one minute stay allowed and appear in one counted row. The count describes grouped records, not refused calls.
- Proposals that wait for your approval.
- Relay notices that were held back.
- A notice that the storage needs a tidy-up while workspaces are open.

### The watchdog

The plugin watches each running job. A job that sends no sign of life for 2 minutes becomes **stalled**. A job that runs longer than its limit becomes **failed**. The limits are 20 minutes for an install or upgrade, 60 minutes for a storage job, and 5 minutes for a workspace start. The message then reads, for example, "Gave up after 60 minutes. Last step: Copying files". A waiting job has no limit. A stalled job that later makes progress returns to running. The check runs in the background, so it works with no browser open.

### Cancel and Dismiss

**Cancel** stops a running install and its helper programs; it appears only where it can stop something, so a storage job or a version check has no Cancel. A cancelled row shows "Cancelled" in grey. **Dismiss** removes a row for a job that ended. You cannot dismiss a running job, so you cannot lose track of live work. You cannot dismiss a proposal. You decide it with **Approve** or **Reject**. You also cannot dismiss an approved action until it has finished, so the record of what you approved stays. If you try, the row tells you why. The tray lives in the server's RAM and starts empty after a reboot.

### The storage tidy-up

When the storage needs a tidy-up and workspaces are open, the tray shows a row with two buttons.

- **Close all and tidy up** closes every open workspace and saves each conversation. The plugin tidies the storage and starts the workspaces again.
- **Later** hides the row for this wait only.

A banner above the terminal says what happens. It reads "Storage tidy-up in progress", "Storage tidy-up starting" or "Storage reclaim needed". It has no action buttons, except the banner "Home can change to plain folders": that one has the button **Convert to plain folders**. Press the arrow at its right to shrink it to a small chip, and press the chip to open it again.

> [!WARNING]
> **Close all and tidy up** closes all your open workspaces. The plugin saves where each one stopped. Do not reboot the server until the banner is gone.

## The Debug Console

### The log viewer

Open **Settings, AI CLI Agents, Debug Console**. The log shows the newest lines and follows new lines by itself. Move the pointer over the log to hold it still while you read. A "Paused" mark shows. Move the pointer away to continue.

Choose a log with the four tabs:

| Tab | What it shows |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Debug** | What the plugin does now. |
| **Migration** | The log of the last upgrade of your settings. |
| **Install** | The log of the plugin install. |
| **Uninstall** | The log of the last removal of the plugin. |

The filters show on the **Debug** tab only.

| Filter | What it does | Default |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Context** | Shows lines from one part of the plugin only, for example one agent. | All |
| **Level** | **ERR! only**, **WARN+**, **INFO+** or **DBUG+**. Each choice also includes the more serious levels. | All |
| **Trace** | Shows one operation from start to end. Type the trace id, for example `t:abc`, then press Enter. | empty |
| **Tail** | How many of the newest lines to load: 100, 500, 1000 or 2000. | 500 |

The undo-arrow icon resets the filters. The copy icon copies the log to the clipboard. The eraser icon clears the selected log after you confirm. You cannot undo it.

### The Performance trace switch

Open the **Support** menu on the Debug Console and tick **Performance trace** to find out why a page is slow or hangs. It is Off by default, and the plugin then writes nothing extra. While it is On, the plugin writes one timing line for each step that takes longer than it should: a slow request, a slow check of the home mount, a slow scan of the Notebook, or a slow save to the boot drive. The lines go to a separate performance log, and a short **WARN** line shows in the **Debug** log, for example "slow: notebook.scan took 640 ms". A fast step writes nothing, so a quiet server writes almost no lines.

Open pages follow the switch when you reload them. Untick the switch when you have finished, and build a support bundle to share what you found.

### The Support menu

Press **Support** to open a menu with four actions and two tick boxes. The second tick box, **Performance trace**, is described in the section above.

1. **Download support bundle**. Expect: a message "Building bundle…", then "Bundle ready" with the file name and size, and the browser downloads a zip file.
2. **Copy forum post**. Expect: a message "Copied!" that reminds you to attach the support bundle yourself. Paste the text into your post on the Unraid forum. Attach the support bundle yourself. The plugin never posts anything.
3. **Create GitHub issue**. Expect: a new browser tab with a prefilled issue on the plugin's GitHub page. Read it. It is only sent when you press submit on GitHub.
4. **Check known issues**. Expect: a panel under the toolbar. It lists matches or says "No known issues matched recent logs" with your version.
5. Tick **Strict anonymize** before an action when you share the result in public. It replaces your share names, your server name and your home network addresses.

#### What the support bundle holds

The bundle is a zip file with these parts: the plugin and Unraid versions, the boot mode, the storage state with a safe list of settings, the layer counts, the last lines of the plugin log and the lifecycle log, the supervisor state, a list of sessions (id, agent and run time), the Activity tray, and the Health result.

The bundle holds no password files and no environment files. It holds no screen content and no folder paths of your workspaces. The plugin cleans every part in several steps: it removes the value of every secret that it knows, removes text that looks like a key, a token, a bearer header, a long hidden string or an email address, and then checks the finished files. If one known secret value remains, the plugin makes no zip. The plugin keeps the newest 5 bundles in RAM and removes older ones.

> [!WARNING]
> The cleaning is thorough but not perfect. Open the zip and read it before you post it in public.

#### What the known-issues check does

The check downloads a short public list that the developer keeps. It compares each entry with the last 500 cleaned log lines. It runs only when you press the button, and the plugin keeps the list for 24 hours. If you are offline, it uses the last copy. A match shows the title, a workaround, the log line that matched, a link to the forum thread and the version that fixes it.

### The copy of the system log

Unraid keeps its system log in RAM, so a reboot or a hard stop loses it. The plugin keeps a copy, so the cause of a lost session can still be found afterwards. Every 5 minutes, when the system log has changed, it writes the last 2 MB of the log to `aicli-syslog-latest.txt`. After a reboot, that file becomes `aicli-syslog-previous-<time>.txt`, and the plugin keeps the newest 3.

By default the copy is in `/boot/logs` on the boot disk. A busy server changes its log all the time, so this rewrites up to 2 MB every 5 minutes. On an old USB stick you can move the copy to a pool, make it less often, or turn it off. There is no control on the page yet. The three settings are on the short list of settings that the plugin management tools may change, so:

1. Turn on **Let agents manage the plugin** (Settings, Configuration, General, Advanced). See [Plugin management tools for agents](agent-tools.md).
2. Ask an agent to change the setting, or run one of these commands in the Unraid terminal:

   ```
   php /usr/local/emhttp/plugins/unraid-aicliagents/src/scripts/admin-agent.php set-setting syslog_keep_location pool
   php /usr/local/emhttp/plugins/unraid-aicliagents/src/scripts/admin-agent.php set-setting syslog_keep_path /mnt/cache/system/aicli-logs
   php /usr/local/emhttp/plugins/unraid-aicliagents/src/scripts/admin-agent.php set-setting syslog_keep_interval_s 1800
   php /usr/local/emhttp/plugins/unraid-aicliagents/src/scripts/admin-agent.php set-setting syslog_keep_location off
   ```

3. Turn **Let agents manage the plugin** off again if you do not use the tools.

The folder on the pool must exist; create it first. A user share, an array disk, and an unassigned or remote disk are refused. While the pool is not mounted, for example while the array is stopped, the plugin keeps no copy and writes nothing into RAM. The change applies at the next copy, without a restart. The files that are already in `/boot/logs` stay there until you remove them.

## The update banner and the reload after an update

When you install a new plugin version, your open terminals keep running the old code until they reconnect. A page reload alone does not fix that. The plugin therefore does both steps in the right order.

1. A banner appears at the top of every open terminal page. It reads "A new version was installed — reconnecting all terminals and reloading in 12s…".
2. The banner counts down. You have two buttons: **Reconnect now** and **Not now**.
3. At zero (or when you press **Reconnect now**), the plugin restarts the terminal connection of every running workspace. Then the page reloads.
4. Expect: your terminals come back on the new code. Your agents and their conversations were not stopped.

**Not now** hides the banner for this update only. A later update shows it again. A page that you open fresh reconnects stale terminals by itself, one time for each version. A tab that returns to the front after a lock screen also looks for an update. The banner stays inside the screen on a phone, and its buttons move below the text.

A workspace that still shows an older version has a small orange dot on its agent icon in the drawer. Hover over the workspace to read why. The panel offers two buttons.

- **Reconnect terminal** connects the browser again. The agent keeps running the old version.
- **Reload** closes the agent, starts it again on the current version, and resumes the conversation. It asks first.

> [!WARNING]
> **Reload** stops the agent. Text that you typed and did not send is lost, and the work in progress stops. The workspace keeps its name, folder, settings, order and Relay identity.

## Choices and settings

| Setting | What it does | Default | When to change it |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Strict anonymize** (Support menu) | Hides share names, server name and home addresses in the bundle and the summaries. | Off | Turn on when you post in public. |
| **Level**, **Context**, **Trace**, **Tail** (Debug tab) | Narrow the log. | All, All, empty, 500 | Narrow it to find one problem. |
| **Let agents manage the plugin** (Settings, Configuration, General, Advanced) | Lets agents read the log and the health. | Off | See [Plugin management tools for agents](agent-tools.md). |
| `syslog_keep_location` (no control on the page) | Where the plugin keeps its copy of the system log: `flash` (`/boot/logs`), `pool` (the folder in `syslog_keep_path`) or `off`. | `flash` | On an old USB stick. See **The copy of the system log** above. |
| `syslog_keep_path` (no control on the page) | The folder on a pool for the copy, for example `/mnt/cache/system/aicli-logs`. It must exist. A user share, an array disk, and an unassigned or remote disk are refused. | Empty | When `syslog_keep_location` is `pool`. |
| `syslog_keep_interval_s` (no control on the page) | Seconds between two copies, from 60 to 86400. | 300 | To write the copy less often. |

The background health check runs every 30 minutes. There is no setting for it on the page.

## What happens behind the scenes

The Health check reads cheap information: files, the mount list and free space. It never changes anything. The Activity tray keeps one small file for each job in the server's RAM and pushes changes to your browser at once. A slow poll is the safety net. For the technical detail, see C4 Component: Platform Foundation and C4 Component: Ajax Gateway Handlers.

## If something goes wrong

| Symptom | What it means | What to do |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| The Health dot is amber or red. | One or more checks are not fine. | Press the (i) next to the dot. Find the check in the table above and follow its advice. |
| An agent upgrade shows **waiting** for hours. | The new version is ready, but a session still runs the old one. | Close that session, or leave it. The upgrade finishes when the last old session ends. |
| A row says "Gave up after 60 minutes". | A storage job ran past its limit. | Read the step in the row. Try the job again after you free room. |
| A merge shows **waiting** with a reason such as "no room". | The merge cannot run until there is enough space. | Free space on the target, or move storage. See [Home and agent storage](storage.md). |
| The boot drive is nearly full. | Old layers, a writable layer on the boot drive, or logs fill it. | Read the **pinned_layers**, **home_upper** and **disk_space** checks. Restart the named workspaces or merge the home. |
| A workspace does not start and the drawer button reads **Emergency Session**. | Home storage is not available. | Check **Settings, Storage** and the drive behind your storage path. An emergency session gives you a temporary home in RAM, and the page shows "Emergency Mode — Temporary home. Work done here is not saved and is lost when storage returns." When storage returns, the session closes and your saved state returns. |
| The Unraid array is stopped. | A workspace whose storage is on flash keeps running. A workspace whose storage is on the array offers Emergency Mode. | Start the array. |
| A home looks damaged. | The layers are broken or lost. | Restore it from a saved copy. See [Home backup and restore](backup-restore.md). |
| A terminal looks old after an update, or has an orange dot. | The terminal connection runs old code. | Press **Reconnect now** in the banner, or **Reconnect terminal** in the hover panel. |
| The page does not reload after an update. | You pressed **Not now**, or the live updates are blocked. | Reload the page by hand. |
| Copy and paste do not work. | Your browser blocks the clipboard on plain HTTP. | Use the manual paste box that shows. See [The terminal](terminal.md). |
| The agent speaks nothing. | The browser needs a click first, or voice is off. | Turn the speaker icon on and click the page. See [Voice](voice.md). |
| A Relay message did not reach an agent. | The agent was busy, so the notice is held. | Look for the pill in the Activity tray. See [Agent Relay](relay.md). |
| An agent says "Plugin management tools are turned off". | The switch is Off. | Turn on **Let agents manage the plugin**. See [Plugin management tools for agents](agent-tools.md). |
| An Unraid page hangs or freezes while the Notebook is on. | The cause is not known yet. | Open **Settings, AI CLI Agents, Configuration**, find the **Notebook** card and set **Notebook** to Off. The page frees up at once. Then open an issue on GitHub (use **Create GitHub issue** in the Support menu) or ask on the forum thread. Say what hung (every Unraid page, or only the plugin pages), how long it lasted, and what your server was doing. If you can, tick **Performance trace** (in the **Support** menu on the **Debug Console** tab) before it hangs again. See **The Performance trace switch** above. |
| A bar at the top says "Your Unraid sign-in has ended". | Your Unraid sign-in in this browser ended, for example after a time-out or a sign-out in another tab. The page stopped asking the server for updates, so it does not fill the server's sign-in limit. | Press **Sign in again**, then sign in. The page opens again. |
| A browser tab shows errors again and again. | The page code is old or damaged. | Reload the page. Check the **client_errors** check. Send a support bundle if it continues. |
| You do not know the cause. | — | Build a support bundle, copy the forum post, and ask on the support thread. |

If the problem is not here, build a support bundle and ask on the forum thread for the plugin, or open an issue on GitHub from the Support menu.
